newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DBS Land seen preparing for Parkway takeover.
newsitem.headline: DBS Land seen preparing for Parkway takeover.

text.p: Singapore property blue chip DBS Land Ltd looks like it is gearing up for a takeover of healthcare group Parkway Holdings Ltd, announcing a major fund raising exercise on Tuesday.

The company said in a statement it aimed to raise Singapore $428 million (US$300 million) by placing out 91.9 million shares at S$4.75 each to "partially finance and refinance its purchase of Parkway shares and to reduce bank borrowings".
"The exercise certainly indicates an intention by the company that it is planning a major acquisition," Lim Chung Chun, investment analyst with ING Baring Securities said.

Last week, the group announced it had agreed to buy 19.2 percent of Parkway for S$391 million, or S$6.50 a share, making it the second largest shareholder in the company after the controlling Tan family with its 24 percent.
Analysts said DBS Land, in which government-linked DBS Bank is a substantial shareholder, is in a comfortable financial position with very little debt.
"In the last few years, its gearing has been falling. Last year, its net debt to equity ratio was 55 percent against the peak in 1993 when it was 119 percent," Lim said.
He said since DBS Land's gearing had been falling, the company need not undertake a major equity fund raising exercise unless it planned a major new investment.

Angeline Ho, investment analyst with Soc-Gen Crosby, said DBS Land would not use all the placement proceeds for the 19.2 percent Parkway stake as the company had earlier said it would use some internal funds to finance the acquisition.
The excess funds raised from the placement would "give the company a bit of leeway in acquiring more shares when the opportunity arises", she said.
The big question is how much more DBS Land will have to pay other major Parkway shareholders to give up their stakes.
Besides the Tans, Malaysia's Ang family controls 14 percent, or 42.29 million Parkway shares. The Angs, long-time friends and partners of the Tans, have said they would sell "if the price is right".
The analysts said DBS Land would most likely have to raise the price by at least 10 to 15 percent above S$6.50 to get the other major shareholders to sell.

An analyst with a European broking firm said that, based on a high of S$7.50, DBS Land would have to fork out another S$2.2 billion for outstanding Parkway shares and warrants if it ends up with 100 percent of Parkway following a general offer.
Under Singapore takeover rules, a general offer would be triggered if DBS Land secured 25 percent of Parkway.
"If DBS Land ends up with 100 percent of Parkway, it would mean their gearing will increase substantially to over 100 percent again -- like in 1993. But they can manage it," the analyst said.
